extra.message: course_blob_shelf_034 writes an attacker-controlled body to an attacker-controlled filename (packet_ref GET parameter / drop_blob.name) via FileSystemStorage.save() with no validation of file type, content, or name. This allows unrestricted upload of arbitrary files into the private_exports/incoming directory by anyone holding the ops token.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: course_roster_fold_034 has no _wrk_gate() call (unlike other ops endpoints) and no authentication, yet exposes internal operational metadata including 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details' and reflects the fold_ref parameter. Any unauthenticated user can access this ops endpoint.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: course_return_lane_151 passes user-controlled input (request.GET/POST 'lane') directly to redirect(lane). An attacker can supply an absolute URL such as 'https://evil.com' to redirect victims to an untrusted site (open redirect).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: course_bundle_thaw_175 calls pickle.loads() on raw request data (request.body or the GET 'blob' parameter, optionally base64-decoded). pickle.loads on untrusted input yields arbitrary remote code execution. The default fallback b"\x80\x04}q\x00." does not mitigate this.

cwe: CWE-502: Improper Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: course_workset_rebind_198 merges an attacker-controlled JSON payload directly into the workset dict via workset.update(payload), allowing the caller to overwrite security-relevant fields such as 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance' that were meant to be server-controlled defaults.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: course_wire_tally_220 logs the full request body and the Authorization header (request.headers.get('authorization')) via logger.warning. This writes bearer tokens and any sensitive request payload into application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: course_digest_fold_278 computes a digest of a user-supplied phrase using hashlib.md5, a broken cryptographic hash algorithm. MD5 is collision-prone and must not be used for security-relevant digests.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: course_identity_ping_338 lacks the _wrk_gate() authentication check present on the other ops endpoints and is reachable by unauthenticated users, allowing anyone to enqueue identity-ping operations and reflect arbitrary handle/channel values.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: course_identity_hint_457 authorizes access by comparing the user-supplied 'verifier' against hardcoded values {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}. These hardcoded credentials are embedded in source and trivially discoverable, enabling authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: course_origin_mirror_467 reflects the attacker-controlled Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permits any malicious origin to issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read the responses, bypassing the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: course_frame_slip_477 explicitly disables browser protections by setting X-XSS-Protection: '0' and clearing the Content-Security-Policy header, weakening the response's defenses against content injection and clickjacking.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: course_jinja_cast_489 builds a Jinja2 template by string-concatenating the user-supplied 'fragment' GET parameter and renders it with Template(...).render(). Because Jinja2's string Template defaults to autoescape=False and evaluates expressions, an attacker can inject '{{ ... }}' payloads achieving server-side template injection / remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: course_shell_probe_501 concatenates the user-supplied 'host' GET parameter directly into an os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) call. Shell metacharacters in host (e.g. '; rm -rf /' or '$(cmd)') yield arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: course_nonce_roll_509 generates a security 'code'/nonce using the random module (random.choice), which is a non-cryptographic PRNG. Tokens/nonces produced this way are predictable and must use secrets (or secrets.token_urlsafe) instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: course_xml_fold_519 parses untrusted request.body with lxml etree.fromstring using a parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks allowing disclosure of local files, SSRF, and denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference ('XXE')

extra.message: course_badge_gate_527 grants an elevated lane (payroll/casework access) based solely on a client-controlled value (the ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header) compared to the constant 'lead'. A client can set this cookie/header to escalate privileges, bypassing server-side authorization.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: course_trace_panel_537 returns internal configuration details to the client, including os.environ.get('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE') and the filesystem path of BASE_EXPORT_DIR, exposing deployment internals to unauthorized actors.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: course_trust_drift_547 disables TLS certificate validation by using ssl._create_unverified_context() when calling urllib.request.urlopen. This makes the outbound HTTPS connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. If deployed without the environment variable, the Django secret key is a publicly known constant, enabling session/CSRF token forgery.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: DEBUG defaults to True (os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'True')). If the environment variable is not set in production, Django runs in debug mode, exposing detailed stack traces, source code, and configuration to attackers.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code

extra.message: The database PASSWORD falls back to the hardcoded default 'postgres' when POSTGRES_PASSWORD is unset. Deployments without the environment variable connect using a well-known credential.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are never set (only HTTPONLY and SAMESITE are configured). Without the Secure flag, session and CSRF cookies are transmitted over plaintext HTTP, exposing them to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: export_grades writes user-controlled fields (sub.student.get_full_name(), sub.student.email) into a CSV via csv.writer.writerow without neutralizing formula characters. A user can set their first_name/last_name (via ProfileForm) to a value beginning with =, +, -, or @, causing formula execution (CSV injection) when an administrator opens the exported grades CSV in a spreadsheet application.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of an Input Parameter Used as a Formula/Command ('CSV Injection')
